jobs.description: EveGuard Chronicles, Eve Security Skip to main content Home About News Blog Careers Login Get Eve now EveGuard Chronicles The Executive Intelligence Series. Each issue is a short read on agentic AI risk and what runtime security does about it, written for the people who have to answer for both. Take the PDF with you. EveGuard Chronicles ISSUE 01 Issue 01 , September 2026 Runtime AI Security for the Agentic Enterprise The case in plain language. Your enterprise is a city you spent a decade walling in, and AI agents now move through it faster than any control built for people can follow: no inventory of what exists, no map of what they touch, no record of what they did yesterday. Then Eve, and what she actually does in the seconds between an instruction and its consequence. The five things she can do with an action, allow, block, redact, alter and interrogate, and the question authorization was never able to ask: not whether an agent may do this, but whether it should be doing it right now. jobs.title: Cookie Information
jobs.description: Cookie Information, Eve Security Skip to main content Home About News Blog Careers Login Get Eve now On this page Introduction What Are Cookies? What Are Scripts? What Is a Web Beacon? Counting Without Cookies Types of Cookies We Use Managing Cookies Contact Information Introduction Our website uses cookies and similar technologies (collectively referred to as “cookies”). Cookies may also be placed by third parties with whom we collaborate. This Cookie Policy explains how cookies work and how we use them. What Are Cookies? Cookies are small text files stored on your device (computer, tablet, or mobile phone) when you visit a website. They help websites remember your preferences, such as: Language selection Login information Device preferences You can manage or disable cookies in your browser settings. Please note that disabling cookies may affect certain website functionalities. What Are Scripts? Scripts are pieces of code used to ensure proper and interactive functioning of our website. They may run on our server or on your device. What Is a Web Beacon? A Web Beacon (or pixel tag) is a small invisible graphic used to monitor website traffic and user interaction. Counting Without Cookies Not everything we measure uses a cookie. We keep a count of how our own pages are used, entirely on our servers. It stores nothing on your device, which is why it is not listed among the cookies below and is not part of the choice you make in the banner. It records daily totals only: the page address, the site that linked to you, any campaign tag in the link, the device type and the country reported by our content delivery network. To count people rather than page views, your IP address and browser identifier are turned into an irreversible code that changes every day, so the same visitor cannot be recognised across two days and the code cannot be turned back into your IP address. Those codes become a plain daily number and are deleted within a week. The privacy policy describes this in full. Types of Cookies We Use 1. Technical / Functional Cookies These cookies are necessary for the proper functioning of the website and to provide services you request. They do not store personally identifiable information. Examples: System Session ID (60 minutes) CookieWarningAgreed (90 minutes) CartStorageID (90 minutes) 2. Statistical Cookies These cookies help us understand how visitors use our website. Data collected is anonymized. 3. Advertising Cookies These cookies allow us and third parties to personalize advertising based on browsing behavior. Because these are tracking cookies, your consent is required before they are activated. 4. Social Media Cookies Social media buttons may store and process data to enable content sharing and personalized advertisements. Managing Cookies You can manage or disable cookies through your browser settings. Instructions are available on the official support pages of your browser provider. If you disable cookies, some website features may not function properly. jobs.title: Information Security Policy
jobs.description: Information Security Policy, Eve Security Skip to main content Home About News Blog Careers Login Get Eve now On this page General Information Security Objectives Principles of Information Security Policy Commitment to Information Security Management General Information Security Objectives The Eve Security general Information Security (IS) objectives related to the information security management system are as follows: Maintaining Integrity of Data and Security Assets Compliance with legislation and contractual requirements Maintaining a safe network (infrastructure and data) Maintaining Vulnerability Management Preventing Unauthorized Access Ensure business continuity by proactively limiting the impact of a security breach Ensuring immediate report of security flaws, breaches. Specific IS objectives (derived from general), the fulfilment, deadlines and responsible persons, are set and monitored. Objectives are monitored regularly and in accordance with set deadlines and business needs. Principles of Information Security Policy Ensure the confidentiality of information and protect it from unauthorized access and misuse, Maintain the integrity of information to ensure its lasting accuracy and applicability, Make information and information systems available to interested parties in accordance with business needs, Build relationships and maintain communication with interested parties by understanding their context and needs and expectations of interested parties, Regularly carry out the identification, analysis, and assessment of information security risks, Plan and take actions based on the results of the regular information security risk assessment, Ensure information security awareness, education, and training for employees and other interested parties, Apply information security measures to ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements, as well as other information security requirements, Ensure appropriate controls and continuous improvement by planning and achieving measurable objectives and monitoring the performance of the system and applied information security measures, Investigate and analyze security incidents and take appropriate actions to address the causes, Investigate and analyze security vulnerabilities and threats and take appropriate actions to address the causes of threats and reduce risks, Develop, maintain, and test recovery plans in order to prevent potential consequences of security incidents and to preserve business continuity if the incident occurs. Commitment to Information Security Management In order to meet these obligations and ensure the appropriate level of controls necessary to demonstrate compliance with the adopted processes, our policy is to maintain a functional and effective information security management system that is established, maintained and permanently improved in accordance with the requirements of the IT Security international standards. The AI security platform for enterprises running autonomous agents at scale. jobs.title: Vulnerability Disclosure
jobs.description: Security Vulnerability Disclosure & Bug Bounty, Eve Security Skip to main content Home About News Blog Careers Login Get Eve now On this page Scope Out of Scope Eligible Vulnerabilities Safe Harbor Rewards How to Report Hall of Fame At Eve Security, protecting our customers' data, AI agents, and runtime environments is our highest priority. We welcome security researchers who help us identify vulnerabilities in our platform. We believe coordinated vulnerability disclosure strengthens the security of the entire AI ecosystem and enables safer adoption of Agentic AI technologies. Scope The following assets are in scope: eve.security Web applications hosted under *.eve.security Public APIs operated by Eve Security Customer-facing SaaS services Out of Scope The following activities are not eligible: Denial of Service (DoS/DDoS) Social engineering of Eve employees Physical security testing Spam-related findings Previously reported vulnerabilities Automated scanning that negatively impacts service availability Vulnerabilities requiring unrealistic user interaction Eligible Vulnerabilities We are particularly interested in findings involving: Authentication and authorization bypass Privilege escalation Sensitive data exposure Cross-site scripting (XSS) Server-side request forgery (SSRF) Remote code execution Business logic vulnerabilities API security issues Multi-tenant isolation failures AI agent abuse or policy bypass Prompt injection leading to unauthorized actions Runtime control evasion techniques Data leakage through AI workflows Safe Harbor If you act in good faith and comply with this policy, Eve Security considers your research authorized and will not pursue legal action regarding your findings. Please: Avoid accessing customer data. Stop testing immediately if sensitive information is exposed. Report vulnerabilities promptly. Give us reasonable time to investigate and remediate issues before public disclosure. Rewards Rewards are determined based on: Severity and impact Quality of report Reproducibility Novelty of the finding How to Report Submit reports to security@eve.security Please include: Vulnerability description Reproduction steps Impact assessment Proof-of-concept screenshots or videos Suggested remediation (optional) Hall of Fame We recognize researchers who help improve the security of AI systems and protect our customers.
